chunks.text: 72-year-old male, Unemployed, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
Spinal anesthesia with bupivacaine and fentanyl, IV paracetamol 1g for perioperative analgesia, and ondansetron 4mg for PONV prophylaxis
Left cataract extraction under local anesthesia in 2019, uneventful

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I’m Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who’ll be looking after you today. I’d like to go through some questions to make sure we’re all set for your hernia surgery. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I’m ready. Let’s get started lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. First, can you tell me a bit about your hernia? How long have you had it, and have you noticed any changes recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: It’s been there for about a year, but it’s gotten bigger and sometimes aches, especially when I lift things. That’s why I’m getting it fixed now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let’s go through your medications. You’re on amlodipine, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin, and paracetamol as needed. Aspirin was stopped recently, right?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I stopped the aspirin a week ago like the surgeon advised. The rest I take daily—amlodipine and lisinopril for blood pressure, atorvastatin for cholesterol, metformin for diabetes, and paracetamol if I have pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, about allergies—your records say ‘no allergies documented,’ but I always like to double-check. Do you have any history of allergic reactions to antibiotics, especially penicillin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes! I had a bad reaction to penicillin years ago. I got a rash all over and hives, so I’ve avoided it since. I think I mentioned it before, but maybe it wasn’t written down properly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. We’ll make sure to note that clearly. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I’ve been fasting since 12am. Just a sip of water for my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Have you had anesthesia before? Any issues with it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Once, for a cataract surgery. I had a spinal then too, and it was fine. No problems at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to know. Lastly, how’s your overall health? Any shortness of breath, chest pain, or difficulty with daily activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk and do most things, but my knees hurt sometimes from osteoarthritis. No breathing issues or dizziness, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for sharing all that, Mr. Tan. We’ll proceed with spinal anesthesia using bupivacaine and fentanyl, plus IV paracetamol and ondansetron as planned. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I think that’s all covered. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] Spinal anesthesia administered with bupivacaine twenty-five milligrams and fentanyl twenty-five micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] Eighteen-gauge IV line placed in left antecubital fossa

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] Airway management: spontaneous breathing, SpO2 ninety-eight percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] Administered IV paracetamol one gram and ondansetron four milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] Hypotension noted, mean arterial pressure sixty-five mmHg, treated with five hundred ml fluid bolus and ten mg phenylephrine IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:45] Surgery completed, patient stable, no residual block

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi Mr Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay lah, a bit sore but manageable. No major pain one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: What would you say your pain level is on a scale of 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 3 or 4? The incision area got some throbbing, but the paracetamol seems to help.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting? We gave you ondansetron to prevent that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, thank God. Stomach is fine, no dizziness or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Breathing comfortable? No shortness of breath or airway issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is okay. Spinal anesthesia made me a bit worried, but I can breathe freely now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Did you experience any awareness or discomfort during the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I was out cold. Woke up only when they moved me to recovery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Your blood pressure and sugar levels are stable. Any knee pain affecting your mobility?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Knees are stiff as usual, but not worse than before. Can bend them slowly.

72-year-old male post-operative from elective open inguinal hernia repair under spinal anesthesia. Surgery completed at 08:45 with stable vitals and no residual block. Intraoperative hypotension (MAP 65 mmHg) managed with fluid bolus and phenylephrine.

Patient has a 1-year history of symptomatic inguinal hernia. Comorbidities include hypertension (amlodipine, lisinopril), diabetes (metformin continued), hyperlipidemia (atorvastatin), and osteoarthritis without functional limitation. Prior uncomplicated spinal anesthesia for cataract surgery. Penicillin allergy (rash/hives). NPO since midnight with sips for morning medications. Aspirin discontinued 1 week pre-op.

Intraoperative management included spinal anesthesia (bupivacaine/fentanyl), IV paracetamol/ondansetron for analgesia/PONV prophylaxis, and transient hypotension responsive to fluid/vasopressor. Anticipated postoperative concerns: hemodynamic instability (spinal anesthesia + antihypertensives), PONV risk despite prophylaxis, glycemic control (diabetes/metformin), and analgesia needs post-spinal anesthesia.

Monitor for hypotension and ensure adequate hydration. Administer scheduled paracetamol and continue PONV prophylaxis. Check blood glucose regularly and maintain current medication regimen (hold metformin only if protocol dictates). Assess pain and consider supplemental analgesia as needed. Document penicillin allergy and confirm NPO status until full awakening.
